findings.summary: The hero entrance (80px rise plus scale over 1.4s) has no prefers-reduced-motion override, so it plays in full for users who asked for reduced motion.
findings.fix: Add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule that removes the translate and scale and leaves either no animation or a short opacity fade.

findings.summary: The background video autoplays and loops forever, with no pause control and no reduced-motion check.
findings.fix: Skip autoplay (show a poster frame) when prefers-reduced-motion is reduce, and add a visible pause/play control.

findings.summary: The parallax scroll listener is not passive and writes a transform on every scroll event, with no requestAnimationFrame throttling.
findings.fix: Register the listener with { passive: true } and batch the transform write in a single requestAnimationFrame per frame (or use a CSS scroll-driven animation).

findings.summary: The scroll-linked parallax layer moves for every user, including those with reduced motion enabled.
findings.fix: Check matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and do not attach the parallax handler when it matches (and listen for changes to the setting).

findings.summary: All 24 cards permanently declare will-change on transform, opacity, top and width, which promotes many layers for no benefit and includes properties that are not compositable.
findings.fix: Remove the blanket will-change, or limit it to transform and apply it only during hover or interaction.

findings.summary: The hover lift animates top (with width also in the transition list), which forces layout on every frame instead of using the compositor.
findings.fix: Animate transform: translateY(-8px) instead of top, and drop width from the transition.

findings.summary: The scroll handler reads getBoundingClientRect and writes style.width on every card in the same loop, which forces repeated layout recalculation on each scroll event.
findings.fix: Replace this with an IntersectionObserver (or read every value first, then write in one requestAnimationFrame), and avoid changing width at all.

findings.summary: The progress bar animates width from an unthrottled, non-passive scroll listener, so it triggers layout on every scroll event.
findings.fix: Set width: 100% and drive transform: scaleX() with transform-origin: left from a passive, rAF-throttled handler or a scroll-driven animation.

findings.summary: The 'Learn more' links are only shown on :hover, so a keyboard user who tabs to a link focuses something with opacity 0.
findings.fix: Also reveal .more on .card:focus-within (or keep the links visible by default).

findings.summary: The links reveal on hover, and touch devices have no hover, so touch users cannot see the links and may tap them by accident.
findings.fix: Keep the links visible by default and wrap the hover-only reveal in @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

findings.summary: button:focus { outline: none } removes the focus indicator from every button and provides no replacement.
findings.fix: Delete this rule and add a visible :focus-visible outline style instead.

findings.summary: Opening the modal does not move focus into the dialog or trap it there, there is no Escape-to-close, and closing does not return focus to the trigger.
findings.fix: Use a native <dialog> with showModal(), or move focus to the email input on open, trap Tab inside the dialog, close on Escape, and restore focus to #open on close.

findings.summary: The open and close setTimeouts are never cancelled, so reopening within 350ms of closing lets the pending timer remove .open and hide the modal that was just reopened, and closing within 20ms of opening can leave it stuck visible.
findings.fix: Store the timer IDs and clearTimeout them in both openModal and closeModal, or listen for transitionend and check the current state before applying it.

findings.summary: The dialog's scale transition has no reduced-motion fallback.
findings.fix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove the scale transform and use only an opacity fade or an instant change.

findings.summary: The counter's requestAnimationFrame loop never stops: it keeps running after the panel is unmounted, and every remount starts another loop.
findings.fix: Keep the rAF handle and call cancelAnimationFrame when the panel unmounts; also stop the count at a target value.

findings.summary: A new IntersectionObserver is created on every mount and never disconnected, so observers pile up and keep holding detached nodes.
findings.fix: Call io.disconnect() on unmount, or unobserve each element once it has received the .in class.

findings.summary: A resize listener is added on every mount and never removed, so listeners accumulate and keep referencing detached counter elements.
findings.fix: Keep a reference to the handler and call removeEventListener on unmount (or use an AbortController signal), or replace it with a CSS media query.

findings.summary: The number keeps changing indefinitely and ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
findings.fix: When reduced motion is preferred, render the final value immediately; otherwise animate to a fixed target and stop.

findings.summary: touch-action: none on html and body blocks native page scrolling and pinch-zoom on touch devices.
findings.fix: Remove touch-action from html and body, and if needed put touch-action: pan-y on the .track element only.

findings.summary: The carousel controls only appear on :hover, so touch users cannot see them.
findings.fix: Keep the controls visible by default, or reveal them on :focus-within as well and restrict the hover-only hiding to @media (hover: hover).

findings.summary: The navigation dots are non-focusable divs with only click handlers, so keyboard users cannot reach or operate them.
findings.fix: Use <button> elements with aria-labels (for example 'Show slide 2') and indicate the current slide with aria-current.

findings.summary: Autoplay advances every 3s without stopping, has no pause control, and ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
findings.fix: Turn off autoplay when reduced motion is preferred, and add a pause/play button plus pausing on hover and focus.

findings.summary: The autoplay interval is never reset after a dot click or swipe, so the carousel can jump to the next slide right after the user picks one.
findings.fix: Clear and restart the interval inside go() on user navigation (or pause autoplay after any user interaction).

findings.summary: The track's slide transition has no reduced-motion override.
findings.fix: Set transition: none on .track under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).
